overall: As of 11:45 ET, Los Angeles is still actively warming at +3.6°F/hr with a running max of 69.8°F — morning patchy fog suppressed early heating, causing a delayed but aggressive ramp-up. Positive acceleration (+0.386°F²/hr) confirms the warming surge is ongoing, not tapering, and the peak is not yet reached despite the intraday model flagging 11:34 ET as a local high-water mark.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is notable: GFS (75.3°F) and HRRR (74.4°F) run 4-5°F above ECMWF (70.2°F) and NBM (69.7°F), with NWS splitting the difference at 73°F. The ECMWF/NBM low end looks increasingly unlikely given that temps are already at 69.8°F with roughly 2 hours of heating remaining before the expected peak (~13:42 ET), suggesting the warmer GFS/HRRR solutions are better capturing today's delayed, fog-delayed heating cycle.
max_temp_prediction: With 69.8°F already in the books at 11:45 ET and active warming velocity still positive, the daily high is nearly certain to clear 72°F and very likely to reach the 72-73°F even bucket — consistent with the NWS 73°F call and the META model's dominant 63.1% probability on that bucket. The 74-75°F bucket (30.1% META) cannot be ruled out if the GFS/HRRR trajectory holds, but the marine influence (SW winds, high dewpoint ~61°F) and fog history argue for a cap near 73°F rather than a full push to 75°F. Confidence is moderate-high for the 72-73°F even bucket as the most likely outcome.
